nodes.summary: For every odd prime $p$ there is a finite $p$-group $G$ of exponent $p^2$ with a subgroup $P$ whose underlying set is exactly the set $\{x^p : x \in G\}$ of $p$-th powers in $G$, such that $P$ is not abelian.
nodes.title: Kourovka 21.137 fails for every odd prime

nodes.summary: The proposition that there is an odd prime $p$ such that for every finite $p$-group $G$ of exponent $p^2$ and every subgroup $P$ of $G$ whose underlying set is exactly the set $\{x^p : x \in G\}$ of $p$-th powers in $G$, the subgroup $P$ is abelian.
nodes.title: Kourovka 21.137, odd-prime form

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ there is a finite $p$-group $G$ with a subgroup $P$ whose underlying set is exactly the set $\{x^p : x \in G\}$ of $p$-th powers in $G$, such that $P$ is not powerful: the commutator subgroup $[P, P]$ is not contained in the subgroup $P^m$ generated by the $m$-th powers of the elements of $P$, where $m = p$ for odd $p$ and $m = 4$ for $p = 2$.
nodes.title: Kourovka 21.137 fails for every prime

nodes.summary: The proposition that there is a prime $p$ such that for every finite $p$-group $G$ and every subgroup $P$ of $G$ whose underlying set is exactly the set $\{x^p : x \in G\}$ of $p$-th powers in $G$, the subgroup $P$ is powerful: its commutator subgroup $[P, P]$ is contained in the subgroup $P^m$ generated by the $m$-th powers of the elements of $P$, where $m = p$ for odd $p$ and $m = 4$ for $p = 2$.
